proof_summary: Induction through the product recurrence shows that both components at index \(n\) are divisible by \(2^k\) whenever \(n\ge 2k+4\), since eventual evenness propagates and each new sum or difference is built from products of highly \(2\)-divisible earlier components. A period-12 computation modulo 15 shows the first component never vanishes, so its first \(k\) prime factors are all 2 and the \(k\)-th prime factor is eventually constant (hence periodic with period 1).
